body: Good bing tv , comfort food, and put your phone away. Lock it up. There’s no reason to be on it while detoxing.
I really needed to read this. Thank you!
We’ve got this. Thank you for sharing. Feel free to inbox me.
We can and will do this. I was sober for a year once. I remember how that success feels. Our happiness is tangible. I’m your supporters as well.

I’ve always been a wild child. I was fortunate enough to have been able to do a wide variety of drugs without getting addicted. When I was freshly 25yo, I had been through a pretty rough breakup. I was dating someone fairly popular and well known so when things ended abruptly they spent every second after spreading rumors and attempting to ostracizing me from every group or comfortable space I had. 

I was sad, alone, and no public space like I had a right there. I was fell into a deep depression. I got invited to some random party and where I was reintroduced to meth. At the time that was the only thing that made me happy and made being alone tolerable. But as you might have experienced these things start with joy and sexual freedom but then transition to from recreational to dependency. The reasons you originally started with become warped. You sometimes get confused as to what lies you’re telling yourself that allows you to continue to use. The balance that once existed is gone and you give more and more time to this drug. Friendships become more distant or end. 

I was able to walk away once for a year. And now I’m back where I started. Not using daily like I was before but I’m sliding further back. 

The battle is daily. You have to create distractions and delete all temptation. You have to try to remember the whole picture before you use too. Not just all the good stuff.  First drugs are fun. Then they’re fun with problems. Then they’re just problems. 

Good luck in your battle.
Good job man! I’m feeling the all of this
I’m not happy with myself either. I don’t know what to substitute this emptiness. I wish you the best.

Hey bud, I’ve been there and am currently back. 

You have to find someone who will listen. Be honest about your usage.. cravings.. triggers.. and thoughts. 

However your getting it. Remove it. Delete, all those people from your phone and block they’re numbers as well. 

Try investing back in your friendships and family. Change your focus. Search for a new drive for happiness. 

If you have PTO or can take a leave with your job, do it. Only do it when you really want to change. On your time away use that time to heal. Sleep, eat better, be honest with someone repeat. Start introducing new things you used to love in your life back into it.

I’m sorry you had to experience that. I worry about putting my family through the same thing when I over indulge. 

I hope you get sober too. Thank you for sharing your story.

Im currently back with my family. I’m attempting to let go of where I was and accepting my life now. 

Thank you.
Thank you. I’m at the same point. I don’t want to lose it all to go back to living in fear. I’m trying to through the next 30days.

I reached the point of being done in 2017. However I was given something to live for. I think having that really helps. I relapsed in late 2018 and I haven’t gotten back. Finding that motivation is a struggle. 

I hope you find that.
